name: Vegetation Dispersion & Garden Preference (pairwise)
description: Faithful replication with the paper's own stimuli: Costa (2022), "Vegetation Dispersion, Interspersion, and Landscape Preference", Frontiers in Psychology 13: 771543. Participants see 40 pairs of residential-garden images side by side (80 images from the paper's Supplementary Data Sheet 1). In 23 pairs only the spacing between plants differs (dispersion: plants spread out vs. clustered); in 17 pairs only the mixing of two plant species differs (interspersion: intermixed vs. separated). Each pair is shown for 10 s, then the images shrink and a 7-point scale appears: three options under the left image, one central "equal" option, three under the right image. Pair order is random per participant and the side of the spaced-out/intermixed image is counterbalanced; a 3-s fixation cross separates trials. Answers are stored per pair as a standardised score from −3 to +3 (positive = prefers the spaced-out / intermixed garden) with the left–right order kept. Original result (56 university students, Bologna): spaced-out layouts preferred in 55% of dispersion trials vs. 33% clustered (mean 0.46, SD 1.83), intermixed preferred in 53% vs. 36% separated (mean 0.28, SD 1.88). Images were created with Realtime Landscaping Architect and are reproduced in the open-access article with permission. Differences from the original study: (1) online on a participant's own screen instead of a 1.25 m projection with a chin rest; (2) no eye tracking (the paper also analysed fixation counts and fixation time); (3) the two familiarisation trials are replaced by a written explanation of the scale; (4) only age and gender are asked; (5) left/right counterbalancing is random half-and-half per participant rather than the paper's fixed scheme.

elements.title: Which of the two gardens do you prefer?
elements.description: Keyed by pair id (e.g. dispersion_01, interspersion_02); shown = [left image, right image]. Value −3…+3 is standardised: positive = prefers the 'high' image (plants spaced out / species intermixed = LOW aggregation), negative = prefers the 'low' image (plants clustered / species separated = HIGH aggregation), 0 = no preference. The raw left–right answer can be recovered from the shown order.

config.description: Participants see 40 pairs of rendered residential gardens side by side. In 23 pairs the plants are spaced out or clustered (dispersion); in 17 pairs two plant species are intermixed or kept apart (interspersion). Each pair is shown for 10 s, then the participant states which garden they prefer on a 7-point left–neutral–right scale. Rebuilt from Costa (2022), Frontiers in Psychology 13: 771543, with the paper’s own 80 images (Supplementary Data Sheet 1).
